key_insight: A mixture of expert neural networks learns data-assimilated flow corrections, achieving axial-compressor predictions close to assimilation accuracy without requiring experimental input during prediction.
engineering_relevance: Learned forcing terms can improve baseline RANS predictions for turbomachinery flows while reducing reliance on experimental measurements during deployment.
method: Fuse experimental PIV with fixed-grid steady RANS and moving-grid hybrid RANS/LES using a Multi-Fidelity Ensemble Kalman Filter.
Train neural networks on the enriched database to map local velocity, velocity gradients and turbulent viscosity to Navier–Stokes forcing terms.
Use a Mixture of Experts to combine learned corrections for different flow regions.
evidence_signal: Against experimental data, the Mixture of Experts shows consistently lower discrepancies than baseline RANS and accuracy very similar to the assimilation results.
watch_item: Individual neural models can produce blade-tip errors exceeding baseline RANS; the abstract does not establish generalization to other geometries or operating conditions.
paper_title: Assisted Turbulence Modeling via Data Assimilation and Machine Learning for Turbomachinery Flows
